query: GPU cloud provider raises or cuts GPU rental prices per hour

results.title: Nebius October Price Increase: Recalculate Startup Runway | Lunera
highlights:
Nebius’s October 1, 2026 on-demand GPU price increases are now effective, with H100, H200, B200 and B300 rates up roughly 17%–21%. Recalculate startup runway using the additional cost of exposed usage—not the headline percentage. A 20% GPU price increase does not mean a 20% increase in company burn, and the price change alone is not a reason to migrate.

...

Source: Nebius public USD on-demand prices, as cited for October 6, 2026. Old → new: H100 $3.85 → $4.50; H200 $4.50 → $5.40; B200 $7.15 → $8.50; B300 $7.85 → $9.50 per GPU-hour.

## The Increase Applies To Specific Resources And Rates

As of October 6, 2026, Nebius’s public pricing page lists these USD on-demand rates per GPU-hour. Percentage increases are calculated from those prices.

| GPU | Old Rate | New Rate | Increase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | 16.9% |
| H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | 20.0% |
| B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | 18.9% |
| B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | 21.0% |

These are per GPU, not per multi-GPU VM, and exclude applicable taxes. The same page shows unchanged on-demand rates for RTX PRO 6000 and unchanged starting prices for L40S configurations.

The change also reaches some CPU-only workloads. Nebius’s compute documentation identifies increases for non-GPU AMD Epyc Genoa CPU and RAM, and non-GPU Intel Ice Lake RAM. Audit those resources separately; do not apply a blanket GPU percentage to the whole invoice. The figures above do not quantify the CPU and RAM increases.

...

Start with billed running time, not GPU utilization. Nebius bills running VM compute by the second; stopped VM compute is not charged, but storage remains chargeable. A running GPU waiting for work still belongs in your cost model.

For each affected GPU type, additional monthly cost equals forecast billed GPU-hours multiplied by the difference between the new and old effective rates.

results.title: Amazon raises reserved AI chip rental prices by about 15% | Superpower Daily
highlights:
Amazon is raising the price of reserved Nvidia AI-chip capacity by about 15 percent, with new rates scheduled for the week after October second, 2026. Quartz, citing MarketWatch, reports that the increase applies to Amazon’s EC2 Capacity Blocks for machine learning: a service that lets customers reserve access to Nvidia hardware, rather than buy the chips outright. The reservations span several generations, from A100 to B300, so the change is not limited to H100s. The bill has two pieces: an upfront reservation fee, plus a separate operating-system fee. So the hourly rate is not the whole cost, and the reservation fee isn’t simply charged one hour at a time. For scale, an eight-chip H100 instance, listed as p5.48xlarge, was priced at about $41.53 an hour in major U.S. regions before the change. Dividing evenly gives about $5.19 per chip-hour, though Amazon does not list that as a separate single-chip rental price. At the old rate, 24 hours comes to about $996.67, before the operating-system fee. Applying exactly 15 percent would put the instance near $47.76 an hour, but that’s a calculation—not Amazon’s confirmed new quote. The increase is approximate, and the actual updated rate for this eight-chip configuration remains unconfirmed until Amazon publishes revised pricing.

...

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

results.title: H100 price per hour, October 2026: 11 clouds compared · ClearCompute
highlights:
The short answer

On 5 October 2026, one H100 80GB SXM listed at $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand across nine clouds, and the Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80. Five specialist clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. The hyperscalers charged $6.88 (AWS), $11.06 (Google Cloud) and $12.29 (Azure), though a three-year commitment brings them down to between $2.97 and $5.40. For an inference server, four things matter as much as the rate: the smallest unit you can rent, egress, billing increments and how fast the price is moving.

...

We read each provider's public price list or pricing API on the same day. Where a provider only sells eight-GPU machines, we divided the machine's price by eight.

| Provider | What you rent | Per GPU-hour | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vast.ai | single GPUs from independent hosts | $1.80 | marketplace median; lowest $1.73 |
| RunPod Community Cloud | one GPU or more | $2.69 | |
| Hyperstack | one GPU or more | $3.20 | |
| RunPod Secure Cloud | one GPU or more | $3.49 | |
| Verda | 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs | $3.77 | $3.37 on 22 September |
| Lambda | 8-GPU instance | $3.99 | $4.29 for a single GPU |
| Nebius | one GPU or more | $4.50 | $3.85 until 1 October |
| CoreWeave | 8-GPU node | $6.16 | North America |
| AWS | p5.48xlarge (8 GPUs) or p5.4xlarge (1 GPU) | $6.88 | us-east-1 |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g (8 GPUs) | $11.06 | us-central1 price table |
| Azure | ND96isr H100 v5 (8 GPUs) | $12.29 | East US |

...

## Why the hyperscalers charge two to three times more#

AWS, Google Cloud and Azure sell their H100s mainly as eight-GPU machines designed for training across many machines at once. The price covers high-bandwidth networking between those machines, plus the rest of the cloud: identity and access controls, private networking, compliance programmes and the support contract you may already have.

A model served from one machine never uses the network between machines. Two H100s in the same server talk over NVLink inside the box.

Hyperscaler list prices also assume you will commit. One year takes 31 to 37% off; three years takes about 56%:

| Provider | On-demand | 1-year commitment | 3-year commitment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AWS (EC2 Instance Savings Plan, no upfront) | $6.88 | $4.33 | $2.97 |
| Google Cloud (resource commitment) | $11.06 | $7.67 | $4.86 |
| Azure (reserved VM instance) | $12.29 | $7.87 | $5.40 |

A three-year AWS commitment lands within 28 cents of the cheapest on-demand H100 we found. That is a good deal if your load is steady, you already spend with AWS, and you are confident an H100 will still be the right GPU for your model in 2029. AWS also cut on-demand P5 prices by up to 45% in June 2025, so $6.88 is already the reduced rate.

...

| Provider | Internet egress |
| --- | --- |
| AWS (us-east-1) | first 100 GB a month free, then $0.09 per GB |
| Azure (East US) | first 100 GB free, then $0.087 per GB |
| Google Cloud (Premium tier) | first 1 GiB free, then $0.12 per GiB ($0.11 above 1 TiB) |
| Lambda, RunPod, CoreWeave, Nebius, Hyperstack | free |

...

Several offerings come only as whole eight-GPU machines: AWS's H200 and B200 instances, Google Cloud's A3 Ultra and A4, Azure's ND H100 v5 and H200 v5, and CoreWeave's on-demand nodes. If your model needs two GPUs and you rent eight at $6.88 each, you pay $55.04 an hour and six GPUs sit idle unless you pack other work onto them. AWS does sell a single H100 (p5.4xlarge) at the same per-GPU rate. Lambda, RunPod, Verda, Hyperstack and Vast.ai rent single GPUs.

| Provider | Spot or preemptible H100 | Below on-demand by |

| AWS (p5.48xlarge, us-east-1, read at 16:26 UTC) | $3.20 | 54% |
| Google Cloud (a3-highgpu-8g) | $6.29 | 43% |
| Azure (ND96isr H100 v5, East US) | $2.27 | 82% |
| CoreWeave | $2.46 | 60% |

## Prices rose this autumn#

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on 1 October: H100 by 17% ($3.85 to $4.50), H200 by 20% and B200 by 19%.
- AWS announced a 15% rise in EC2 Capacity Block prices from 7 October, taking a P5 H100 from $5.19 to $5.97 per GPU-hour.
- Verda's H100 went from $3.37 on 22 September to $3.77 on 5 October, up 12% in 13 days, according to the Wayback Machine's captures of its price page.

Any price survey goes stale within weeks, this one included. For today's number, live trackers such as gpufinder.dev, which polls 22 vendors every hour, and SkyPilot's GPU Compass are better sources. A survey is more useful for explaining what the number buys.

results.title: B300 SXM Up 6.2% in GPU Rental Market — Week of September 28 - October 4, 2026 | AIMC | AIMC
highlights:
B300 SXM posted the largest week-over-week median price increase among tracked SKUs, rising 6.2% from $7.96 to $8.45 per GPU-hour in the week ending October 4, 2026 — a move that widened the spread between Blackwell-generation hardware and legacy Ampere inventory. According to AIMC observations across 36 reporting marketplaces and 7,933 discrete price points, the B300 gain arrived while its Blackwell sibling, the B200 SXM, advanced a more modest 1.5% to $6.79, and the H100 SXM added 2.2% to $3.49. The divergence within and across GPU generations — with inference-oriented SKUs like the L40S and L4 both slipping marginally — represents the structural pattern most worth examining in this report. What follows is a segment-by-segment breakdown of pricing behavior across 119 distinct SKUs.

...

- 36 authorized marketplace partners contributed pricing data this week. Full list at aiminingco.com/data-partners.
- Largest week-over-week decliner: L40S at -1.2% ($1.59 → $1.57 median across covered marketplaces).
- Largest week-over-week gainer: B300 SXM at +6.2% ($7.96 → $8.45 median across covered marketplaces).

## Headline Movements

| GPU | Last Week Median | This Week Median | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 SXM | $7.96 | $8.45 | +6.2% |
| RTX A4000 | $0.29 | $0.30 | +3.0% |
| H100 SXM | $3.42 | $3.49 | +2.2% |
| B200 SXM | $6.69 | $6.79 | +1.5% |
| L40S | $1.59 | $1.57 | -1.2% |

...

This week's data spans 36 marketplaces with 7,933 total listing observations across 119 distinct GPU SKUs.

H100 pricing ranged from $1.00/hour at ionet to $10.00/hour at huggingface across 25 marketplaces.

B200 pricing ranged from $3.69/hour at deepinfra to $8.19/hour at togetherai across 15 marketplaces.

L40S pricing ranged from $0.81/hour at hydrahost to $2.48/hour at qubrid across 12 marketplaces.

A100 pricing ranged from $0.78/hour at synpixcloud to $3.34/hour at cirrascale across 19 marketplaces.

...

The most striking pattern in this week's dataset is not where prices sit, but how wide they vary for the same hardware. AIMC's data shows that the L40S — a single SKU tracked across 12 marketplaces — carried median prices ranging from $0.81 to $2.48 per GPU-hour during the week of September 28 through October 4, a spread of more than 3x between the cheapest and most expensive observed listings. The H100 family tells a similar story, with prices spanning $1.00 to $10.00 across 25 marketplaces. Spreads of this magnitude, for identical or near-identical hardware, suggest these segments have not yet developed the price convergence typically associated with mature, liquid commodity markets. Where buyers and sellers have broad, transparent access to comparable alternatives, spreads tend to compress. Wide spreads may instead reflect fragmented discovery, differing contract structures, or regional supply concentrations — though with one week of data we cannot reliably distinguish which factor dominates.

By contrast, the week-over-week price movements themselves were comparatively contained. Ai Mining Co. tracked a +6.2% gain in B300 SXM median price (from $7.96 to $8.45), the largest single mover in this period, while most other SKUs shifted by less than 1%. The RTX A4000 moved from $0.29 to $0.30, a +3.0% change that is statistically notable but economically narrow in absolute terms. Whether the B300 SXM move reflects a genuine demand signal or listing noise across a thinner sample is something a single week's observation cannot resolve.

results.title: The H100 can cost 9x more depending on where you buy it. | Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
Here are 3 things that stood out:

1. The 9x price spread

An H100 80GB can range from $1.30/hr on unreserved marketplace capacity to $12.29/hr on hyperscaler enterprise infrastructure.

That's a 9.45x difference for the same class of GPU.

2. H100 prices aren't falling everywhere

On October 1, Nebius AI Cloud increased its HGX H100 on-demand rate from $3.85 → $4.50/hr — a 16.9% increase.

As newer Blackwell GPUs enter the market, Hopper pricing isn't following a simple downward curve.

3. $/GPU-hour can be a misleading metric

The rate card is only part of the bill.

Depending on the provider and deployment, buyers may also need to account for:

• Data egress charges
• Virtualization overhead
• Storage • Networking
• Minimum node commitments
• Spot/preemptible risk

For example, some providers require entire 8-GPU nodes, meaning the headline “per GPU” price doesn't tell the whole story.

results.title: GPU Clouds in 2026: H100s at $2.59 an Hour, $104B of CoreWeave Backlog on $35B of Debt, and a Six-Year Bet on Silicon · Ajay Kumar
highlights:
The headline everyone remembers is the fall. In spring 2023 an eight-GPU AWS P5 node listed above $60 an hour, about $7.50 per H100-hour, per emma.ms's provider survey. Coloprice's compilation of Silicon Data's index puts mid-2023 at roughly $8, 2024 at $3 to $5, the first half of 2025 at $2 to $3, and the October 2025 trough at $1.70, when the market briefly believed Blackwell would make Hopper worthless. SemiAnalysis's December 2023 model had shown that an operator paying 13 percent interest needed about $1.53 an hour to cover an H100 server's capital and hosting, which is why $1.70 was a floor.

Less reported is the rebound: $2.00 in December 2025, $2.20 four weeks later, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index at $2.35 in March 2026, Silicon Data around $2.53 by mid-year. Ornn's OCPI-H100, a volume-weighted index of transacted neocloud H100 SXM rentals rather than rate cards, printed $2.59 per GPU-hour on 4 October 2026, with a three-month range of $2.46 to $3.17. The operators say the same. CoreWeave told its Q2 2026 call that prior-generation pricing "is at or above where it was years ago", that it raised list prices about 25 percent in July, and that it had signed an A100 contract, a 2020 architecture, running into 2029. Nebius's Q2 letter reports deals above $20 million of annual revenue per megawatt and "more than 30% higher pricing on older-generation GPUs versus Q1".

...

The spread between the transacted index and the rate cards is the second thing to notice. Here is what the public price pages said on 5 October 2026, per GPU per hour, before any negotiated discount.

| Provider, page fetched 5 Oct 2026 | H100 SXM $/GPU-h | H200 | B200 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CoreWeave, HGX 8-GPU | $6.16 on-demand, $2.46 spot | $6.31 | $8.60 | GB200 NVL72 $10.50 per GPU |
| Lambda, 8-GPU | $3.99 ($4.29 single) | not listed | $6.69 | reserved via sales |
| Nebius | $3.85, rising to $4.50 from 1 Oct | $4.50 to $5.40 | $7.15 to $8.50 | preemptible from $0.79 |
| Together | $3.99, $3.19 at 91 to 180 days | $5.99 | $8.19 | GB200 "contact" |
| RunPod | $2.69 community, $3.49 secure | $3.59 / $4.59 | $5.98 / $6.79 | community = third-party hosts |
| Vast.ai, public offers API, 1x on-demand | low $1.98, median $3.79, 6 offers | n/a | n/a | query I ran on 5 Oct |
| OCPI-H100 transacted index | $2.59 on 4 Oct, 30-day -10.4% | n/a | n/a | volume-weighted neocloud trades |

SF Compute's market page redirects to a login and Shadeform's directory is client-rendered, so both are absent rather than guessed. The pattern is clear anyway: on-demand list is $3.85 to $6.16 at the integrated neoclouds, the marketplace floor is around $2, the transacted average is $2.59, and the newest silicon carries roughly a 2x premium (B200 at $6 to $8.60, GB200 at $10.50) because buyers pay for tokens per dollar, not hours. Nebius's 1 October increase and CoreWeave's July rise are the first across-the-board list price rises since 2023.

results.title: Small GPU Rental Providers vs Large Clouds | Noach Ark
highlights:
The following public rate examples were checked on October 5, 2026. They are in USD, before applicable taxes and additional charges. They do not establish available stock or equal performance.

Public GPU rental rate examples checked October 5, 2026, in USD

| Provider and product | Configuration and price basis | Observed public rate | Important condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod Secure Cloud Pods | RTX 4090, 24 GB; one-GPU rate | $0.74/hour | Storage is additional; verify the selected region and offer |
| Runpod Secure Cloud Pods | H100 SXM, 80 GB; one-GPU rate | $3.49/hour | Pod compute price, distinct from serverless or cluster pricing |
| Hyperstack on-demand | H100 SXM, 80 GB; per-GPU rate | $3.20/hour | Confirm the VM flavor, CPU/RAM allocation, region, and extras |
| Lambda one-GPU instance | H100 SXM, 80 GB | $4.29/GPU/hour | Rate is for the one-GPU configuration |
| Lambda eight-GPU instance | Eight H100 SXM GPUs, 80 GB each | $3.99/GPU/hour; $31.92/node/hour calculated | Renting the whole node is required for that configuration |
| AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks | p5.4xlarge, one H100; US East, N. Virginia | $5.191/instance/hour effective rate | Scheduled reservation product; not an ordinary on-demand quote |

Sources: Runpod pricing, Hyperstack pricing, Lambda instance configurations, and AWS Capacity Blocks pricing. Runpod's Secure Cloud option was selected when checking its Pod rates. The AWS example has a named region; the specialist pages' displayed rates do not establish stock in a matching region.

Example: a developer with twenty hours of experiments. If the intended job fits and performs adequately on the quoted Runpod RTX 4090 configuration, twenty billed hours at the observed rate cost $14.80 for compute. This is an arithmetic estimate, not a measured job duration. A small bill can be attractive for experiments, but model memory, software compatibility, and acceptable completion time must be verified first. A lower-cost GPU cannot replace an H100 workload merely because both offers are called GPU rentals.

results.title: H100 SXM median closed at $3.49 on CME's futures date, October 2026
highlights:
The figure$3.49 Weekly H100 SXM median, week of September 28, 2026, final · $3.49 per GPU-hour, 31 quotes at 29 providers, index 102.6 · read Oct 4, 23:40 UTC · source · live page

...

The week of September 28, 2026 closed at midnight UTC on October 5 with a median of $3.49 per H100 SXM GPU-hour, taken over 31 publicly listed on-demand rate cards at 29 providers, each linked to the page it was read from. October 5 is also the date CME Group gave, in its release of August 11, 2026, for listing two cash-settled contracts on NYMEX, Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures and Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures, pending regulatory review. Intercontinental Exchange announced GPU compute futures on Ornn’s OCPI on May 19, 2026, with no listing date in that release.

...

A futures contract pays out against the index it is settled on. CME’s release names Silicon Data’s hourly rental indices as the settlement reference, and Ornn’s published methodology computes its OCPI from executed rental prices, which an outside reader cannot check one by one. The figure above is a different thing: the median of what providers publicly ask for an H100 SXM hour, each rate in the week’s receipts with its source page and read time. The two can print different numbers in the same week and both be correct. This site does not reprint either settlement index, because their terms do not allow it, and issues no contract of its own.

For a reader who pays for GPU hours, the practical difference is the check. A price in this index can be opened at the provider’s own page; a settlement value is a number its publisher states. The panel matters as much: in the week of September 28 the four hyperscaler H100 quotes had a median of $9.90 against $3.20 for the 27 quotes at 25 specialist clouds, so whether a panel counts AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle moves an H100 median on its own. For the second contract’s card, the B200 page printed a median rate card of $6.89 across 32 rate cards on October 5.

## Why the median fell and the index rose in the same week

The week before, September 21, closed at $3.70 over 26 quotes at 24 providers, index 100.4. From $3.70 to $3.49 the median fell; from 100.4 to 102.6 the index rose, or 102.6 / 100.4 = 1.022. The two columns answer different questions. The index links only the quotes read in both weeks, so it moves when a cloud changes a price. The median moves with who is in the basket.

Five quotes entered, and all five sit below the old median: Taiga Cloud at $2.60 (an advertised from rate), GPU.ai at $2.95, GEODD at $3.00, Edgevana at $3.07 and Thunder Compute at $3.20. Each entered because we first read that page during the week, between September 29 and October 4, not because a provider cut a price. None left.

Of the 26 quotes read in both weeks, four moved, all upward. JarvisLabs went from $2.69 to $3.49, first read at the new rate on October 4 at 19:40 UTC; our module for that page was not changed in those days, so the move is on the page. Nebius is among the four too, but that step comes from our parser switching to the column Nebius published for October on October 1, which a piece of October 2 describes.
